internal injuries and head trauma.

At 8:47 a.m. on November 7, 2024, Employee #1 was working on a roof attempting
to locate and repair a leak. While on the roof, he fell through a skylight and

At 10:15 a.m. on November 8, 2024, Employee #1 was performing landscaping work

The mower and employee veered off the lawn and fell approximately 15 feet into

asphyxiation caused by drowning.
At 9:00 a.m. on October 23, 2024, Employee #1 was working in a
climate-controlled office when she lifted a box full of papers to be shredded.
While carrying the box, it shifted in her arms, and she felt a pull in her back.
The employee continued to work but later experienced complications from the back
injury.  She was hospitalized and later died.
At 7:20 p.m. on November 1, 2024, Employee #1 had just finished dumping the
first load and pulled the truck forward to dump the rear trailer. Afterward, the
employee went to the cat-walk. A fellow trucker noticed that Employee #1 was
taking an unusually long time and went up to investigate. The trucker found
Employee #1 unresponsive on the cat-walk and immediately notified the site
employer. Chest compressions were started, an AED was hooked up, and emergency
responders were called. Despite efforts to revive Employee #1, the employee
died.  The cause of death was suspected to be a heart attack or heart failure.
At 10:22 a.m. on November 8, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a trash removal
company, was operating a trash truck when he became caught between the truck and
a telephone pole. The employee was unable to breathe due to the crushing force

At 11:30 a.m. on November 14, 2024, Employee #1 was cutting a 4-inch cast iron
pipe with a gas-powered saw. The saw blade jammed, causing the saw to kick back
and strike him in the neck. He sustained a fatal laceration from the rotating
saw blade.

called, but the employee was pronounced dead at the scene due to the injuries
sustained.
At 9:45 a.m. on July 8, 2024, an employee was spotting a semi-trailer to
position in front of a crane outrigger.  The employee was caught between the
semi-trailer and the outrigger.  The employee was killed due to blunt force
trauma to the torso.
At 11:08 a.m. on November 5, 2024, Employee #1 was working at the site of a
one-story residential structure being demolished with a trackhoe. The building
was constructed of concrete block. During demolition, a portion of the block
wall collapsed and struck him. He sustained fatal injuries.
At 12:00 a.m. on November 8, 2024, Employee #1 was working alone while
performing a pre-work inspection of the roof on a two-story single-family
residence that had been damaged by a fallen satellite dish. He was using an
Archom 16-foot aluminum telescopic ladder to access the roof above the garage
from the front of the residence. The eave height on the front (northern) side of
the garage was approximately 14 feet, with a 9/12 pitch. The ladder, which was
fully extended, reached only one to two rungs above the fascia board. While
transitioning either onto or from the roof, Employee #1 fell approximately 14
feet to the concrete driveway. He sustained fatal blunt force injuries to the
upper torso and head and was killed.
At approximately 7:00 a.m. on July 25, 2024, Employee #1, a Field Service
Representative (FSR), was loading a Ryder 26ft refrigerated box truck with the
lift gate raised. A coworker lowered the left gate to assist Employee #1.
Employee #1, unaware the gate had been lowered, stepped out while carrying two
boxes and fell to the ground. Emergency services were contacted, and Employee #1
was transported to the hospital. On July 26, 2024, Employee #1 died from blunt
force trauma to the head and neck.
At 2:30 p.m. on November 12, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a recycling company,
was attempting to clear debris below a conveyor belt when the machine
unexpectedly activated, causing the employee to be crushed. The employee
suffered blunt trauma from the crushing incident and was later pronounced dead.

move a non-operational bobcat skid loader onto a flatbed trailer using a winch

piece of wood to assist with the loading process. Upon returning, the coworker

load arm and tire/body. The center/tilt cylinder had been broken off the skid
loader but was still attached to the winch system. Employee #1 sustained head
trauma, which ultimately led to his death.

forks of the machine to guide the tree down while a coworker cut the tree with a
chainsaw. As the tree was cut, the weight of the tree against the forks caused
the telehandler to tip over. Employee #1 was thrown from the machine and was
subsequently crushed by it, sustaining fatal crushing injuries.

ditches to create a fire line for a forest fire. Employee #2 fell a tree, and as

injury involving a blade. The incident occurred at the worksite and was

hydraulic cylinder and ram of a baler located on the west wall of the Baler
Room. It was believed that the baler machine may have been cycled to extend the

At 1:00 p.m. on December 27, 2024, Employee #1 was replacing a multi-piece tire

space and attempted to sit down on the bleachers when he collapsed. It was

At 9:30 p.m. on January 26, 2025, Employee #1 was working for an advertising

injured due to multiple traumas.
At 6:34 p.m. on January 9, 2025, Employee #1 was working as a bus transit
operator for a public transportation department. It was the end of his shift and
Employee #1  had just arrived at the bus parking lot where he was removing the
money vault from the bus.  Employee #1 was walking into the office when  a
coworker, the senior systems transportation supervisor, heard a noise like
something had fallen and yelled out Employee's name and proceeded to
investigate. The coworker saw that  Employee #1 had fallen onto the ground. The
coworker called 911 and attempted resuscitation until  first responders arrived
on scene to take over. Paramedics transported the employee to the hospital,
where he was pronounced dead.
At 9:30 p.m. on October 27, 2024, an employee, a full-time laborer employed by
Vector Energy Technologies, LLC, was walking behind a backhoe loader moving in
reverse on a two-lane road at the Underground Construction Company project site.
The loader, a CAT Model 420F2, struck and ran over the employee's lower body
with its rear tire. The employee was on his first day at the worksite. A witness
approximately 30 yards away heard the loader backing up and saw the employee
walk directly into its path. Emergency medical services transported the employee
to the hospital, where he was admitted with severe internal injuries. The
employee later died from the injuries.
On January 21, 2025, Employee #1 was working as a truck driver for a freight
company and was driving on a highway carrying materials to a jobsite.  Employee

contractor and were meeting in the human resources office. The office is located

president, and the director of human resources. During this meeting, one of the
employees who worked as an accountant opened fire, firing several shots. The

the age and release the check-out lane so the customer could finish checking

medical condition.

fatally injured.
At approximately 4:30 a.m. on July 30, 2024, Employee #1 was picking orders in
the warehouse when they suddenly collapsed in the aisle. Emergency services were

At 10:50 a.m. on October 14, 2024, Employee #1, a truck driver for a

was walking along the far side of the trailer, out of view of the equipment

resulted in a fatality.
At 5:30 p.m. on January 22, 2025,  Employee #1 had been working as a machine
operator for a manufacturer of cementitious construction blocks.  A coworker
found Employee #1 unresponsive in his personal vehicle parked across the street
from the work site following his work shift.  At the time he was found, Employee
#1 was not engaged in any work-related activities.  It was determined that
Employee #1 died from probable atherosclerotic heart disease.
At 6:45 a.m. on January 14, 2025, Employee #1 working as a sales worker for a
hardware store and was setting up ceiling lights and fans display. Employee #1
fell onto the concrete floor.  Employee #1 died from head and neck injuries.
At 1:44 p.m. on January 27, 2025, Employee #1 was working as a wing walker for
an airline and had just removed a tow bar from an aircraft that was pushed back
to the taxi way area of the ramp.  Employee #1 was on his way back to the
airport gate.  As he was walking back to the gate ahead of the tug, he was
struck from behind by the same tug that had just released the aircraft. Employee
#1 died from chest trauma.
On January 18, 2025, Employee #1 was  working for a charitable organization and

While inside the vehicle,  Employee #1 was on the phone with a friend  until she

with blood on her face. Emergency services transported the employee to the

At 3:35 p.m. on November 1, 2024, Employee #1 was performing training exercises
in a swimming pool when he suffered a suspected heart attack. Emergency
responders were called to the scene. Despite lifesaving efforts, the employee
died.
At 2:00 p.m. on November 1, 2021, Employee #1 was working with others to move
railroad cars loaded with logs using a trac mobile on a rail spur. During the
operation, the trac mobile and the first loaded railcar derailed and overturned.
As the employee jumped off the trac mobile, logs spilled from the derailed
railcar and struck him. Emergency medical services responded, but the employee
was pronounced dead at the scene.
At 12:45 p.m. on October 30, 2024, Employee #1 was loading a decoiler machine
with a metal coil weighing approximately 2,000 pounds. While preparing to load
another coil, he noticed the previous coil was still in the process of
decoiling. He attempted to bring the coil back toward himself to place it back
on the stand. After setting the coil down and removing the hook that was
securing it, the coil shifted and fell, pinning him to the ground. Employee #1
sustained a severe laceration to his left arm, a ruptured spleen, and a
fractured T-11 vertebra, which resulted in his death.
At 9:00 a.m. on August 13, 2024, Employee #1 and a coworker were inside the
basket of a Genie boom lift when Employee #1 made contact with an energized hot
wire. Employee #1 sustained fatal injuries due to electrocution.
At 10:00 a.m. on November 13, 2024, Employee #1 was inside a large section of
HVAC duct applying Design Polymerics DP 2590 Duct Liner Spray Adhesive to repair
sagging insulation. After completing the adhesive application, Employee #1 used
a Talon pin welder to secure the insulation. While using the welder, a spark
ignited flammable vapors from the adhesive, causing a flash fire inside the
duct. Employee #1, who was engulfed in flames, exited the duct.   Coworkers used
a fire extinguisher to put out the flames. A coworker working in the opposite
corner also jumped out to safety. Employee #1 sustained burns to over 80% of his
body and later died from complications related to the injuries.
At 12:45 a.m. on November 13, 2024, Employee #1 and a coworker were installing
subflooring on the second level of a residential home above the garage,
approximately 12 feet from the ground. Employee #1 was gluing and screwing the
subfloor down to the trusses while Employee #1 handed him subfloor panels.  The
coworker reported hearing a cracking sound, then observed 20 roof trusses on the
left side of the home's second level-each measuring approximately 25 feet 4
inches-beginning to collapse. Employee #1 was crushed by the collapsing roof
trusses and sustained fatal blunt force trauma to the head and body.
At approximately 3:00 p.m. on November 12, 2024, a process cooker at a facility
overpressurized and exploded. The explosion resulted in twelve employees being
hospitalized, including one employee who later died from injuries sustained
during the incident. At approximately 1:00 a.m. on November 13, 2024, a second
employee was found dead in the laboratory area of the facility, having been
discovered several hours earlier. The incident remains under investigation.
At 3:40 p.m. on November 11, 2024, Employee #1 was working from a 6-foot step
ladder while setting joists in place from the first story of a structure. He
stood on the top of the ladder, lost his balance, and fell to the concrete
floor. He sustained fatal head trauma upon impact with the concrete.
At 8:42 p.m. on November 11, 2024, an employee working as an assembler for a
slaughterhouse was using a straight knife to cut product before letting the
piece fall into a conveyor. During the cut, the employee struck himself in the
clavicle near the right side of his neck causing heavy bleeding. The employee
turned to coworkers working on the same table for help. The coworkers stopped
the line and rendered aid, holding the employee to prevent him from falling
until the nurse arrived. The employee died from the inability to breathe due to
the nature of the cut.
At 9:45 a.m. on November 4, 2024, an employee working as a laborer for an
aluminum processor was cutting the branches of a tree with a chainsaw. The vines
had not been removed before starting the cuts. Vines fell onto the employee's
face, and while trying to remove them with the chainsaw, he cut the sling that
was being used to secure the platform where he was working. The employee fell
and was struck by the falling basket. The employee died from multiple trauma
including fractures, lacerations, and cuts.
At 10:30 a.m. on November 13, 2024, an employee working as a the mechanic shop
foreman for an automobile parts store had just returned from his morning break.
The employee and a coworker working as a foreman had begun working on a vehicle
together. The employee began working under a customer's Chevrolet Titan 90 farm
truck by himself. The employee was reinstalling a steering cylinder that was
located under the engine and next to the front axle of the truck. The truck was
resting on wooden blocks that were positioned under the wheel hubs. The truck
had been positioned this way since the steering cylinder had been removed
approximately 6 days prior. Based on the evidence documented it did not appear
the employer took any measures to ensure the blocking was secured against
unintentional movement, such as preventing the steering wheel from moving
laterally, or a means of preventing the blocks from "Kicking out." Soon after
this work resumed, the truck came off the blocks and landed on top of the
employee crushing him. Coworkers elevated the truck with a hand pumped jack at
which time they noticed that the employee had sustained a head injury from
impact with the oil pan under the truck. The employee also sustained blunt
trauma to his chest from the axel. The employee died as a result of his
injuries.
At 9:37 a.m. on November 14, 2024, an employee working as a welder for a rail
transportation services company was welding on a locomotive electrical cabinet.
After the employee appeared to have completed the weld, he laid aside the
two-step ladder he was using before collapsing. The employee died, but the cause
of death and if there was an injury or illness associated with his death has not
yet been determined.
At 1:30 p.m. on November 13, 2024, Employee #1 was operating an empty
2,000-gallon water truck, driving to a new staging area. While navigating a
curve, the truck struck a guardrail and rolled approximately 100 feet down an
embankment, striking trees and rocks before coming to a stop. Employee #1
sustained fatal injuries in the rollover incident.
At 7:45 a.m. on November 16, 2024, an employee working as a for a full-service
restaurant chain was attempting to retrieve mobile pan racks that are stored on
the patio roof at the back deck near the dumpster area. The mobile pan racks are
used during each holiday season. According to a coworker assisting the employee,
the employee was up on the roof when he unexpectedly decided to descend the
ladder without taking any of the pan racks. The employee was climbing down the
ladder from the 10-foot elevated back deck and was possibly on the fourth or
fifth rung when he lost control. The ladder swung to the right and the employee
fell backward striking his head on the concrete floor. The coworker confirmed
that the ladder was not secured at the top and that no one was holding it on the
ground while the employee was descending. Due to the uneven concrete surface in
the dumpster area, the coworker stated that they placed the ladder legs on two
kitchen rags for stability. The ladder was not authorized for use at the
restaurant and had been left behind by a painting contractor. The employee died
from blunt force trauma to the head.
On or about August 30, 2024, to September 1, 2024, an employee working as a line
cook for a full-service restaurant was stocking food in a walk-in cooler. The
employee slipped and fell in the cooler and hit her left calf and/or knee during
the fall. The employee sustained traumatic compartment syndrome in the leg. On
September 28, 2024, the employee was hospitalized for 41 days due to
complications from the injury. On November 10, 2024, the employee died.
At 4:15 a.m. on October 31, 2024, Employee #1 was walking from the back of his
work truck to enter the driver's seat. The truck was parked on the right
shoulder of an interstate where a three-employee crew was removing traffic signs
from the roadside. A semi-truck and trailer swerved onto the shoulder past the
white line and struck Employee #1. He sustained fatal injuries as a result of
the incident.
At 1:38 p.m. on March 17, 2023, Employees #1 and #2 were sheathing the roof of a
3-story townhome. Employee #1 stepped onto an unsecured platform elevated next
to the eave, which was hooked onto the mast of a telehandler and already
occupied by Employee #2. When Employee #1 stepped onto the platform, it tipped
off the mast and fell approximately 30 feet to the ground with both employees on
it. Employee #1 struck his head on the concrete floor of the garage and died
from his injuries. Employee #2 landed on the graded ground and suffered

respiratory issues. On the morning of November 18, 2024, a roommate found the
employee dead. The cause of the employee's death is unknown and is possibly due
to an adverse reaction to inhalation of blast media and materials which included
coal slag, steel grit and paint particles from the materials that were being
removed.
At 11:00 a.m. on November 11, 2024, an employee working as a mechanic/welder for
an automotive shop was using a a plasma cutter to cut the top off a 55-gallon
metal drum. The employee was unaware the drum contained flammable liquids. The
instant the plasma cutter touched the drum, the drum exploded upwards and came
to rest in the adjacent stall. The explosion caused a localized fire due to the
flammable liquid in the drum. The employee was sustained multiple contusions and
burns to his abdomen, face, chest and arms in the explosion. The employee was
flown to the emergency department of a medical center. At 6:52 p.m. on November
19, 2024, the employee died from his injuries.
At 11:22 a.m. on November 14, 2024, an employee was working as a construction
laborer for a demolition contractor. The employee and two coworkers were
assisting the general contractor and another subcontractor. While they were
doing their assigned work under their own contract, the general contractor was
working with the other subcontractor on flooring behind the Interkal friction
power operated telescopic seating bleachers. The general contractor requested
assistance from the employee and two coworkers to move the bleachers. As the
crew was pushing the bleachers, the rear section of the structure failed and
landed on the employee and one of the coworkers for the other subcontractor. The
employee died from crushing injuries and was retrieved by the County Coroner.
The supervisor was on site but did not witness the incident.
At 1:57 p.m. on November 20, 2024, an employee of Linco Fab Inc was working from
the ground when a steel column measuring 26 feet long, 14 inches wide, and 5.5
inches deep fell on the employee. The column was anchored by two bolts. The
employee was fatally crushed by the falling steel column.
At 10:36 a.m. on November 19, 2024, an employee working as a landscaper for a
landscaping contractor was working up in a large oak tree designated as needing
trimming to maintain adequate distance from a electrical power lines. The
employee was wearing a harness and climbing gear but fell approximately 35 to 40
feet to the ground. The employee was transported to the hospital but died from
multiple blunt trauma from impact with the ground.
At 5:00 p.m. on November 20, 2024, an employee working for an oil company was
performing maintenance on a 2-phase separator vessel. The vessel  was undergoing
clearance testing of the system maintenance was performed due to a paraffin
buildup. The employee was working by the tank battery venting the pressure out
of the vessel. The employee vented pressure out through a pipe that hung down
from the vessel with an L-bend at the bottom. When the employee vented the
pressure out of the pipe, it caused the pipe to rotate around its point of axis.
As the pipe was on the downward swing, it struck the employee who was standing
in the path of rotation in the head. The employee died from skull fractures and
other head trauma including fractures, contusions and a concussion.
At 12:21 p.m. on November 20, 2024, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were working as
telecommunications repair installers for a telecommunications provider. The crew
was investigating a mystery wire that was uncovered by a homeowner in the back
yard of a residence. The crew was tryin to determine if the wire was a data
cable or not. Employee #1 tested the wire and the meter indicated that there
were 0 volts running through the wire. Employee #1 then retrieved a tool to cut
a "window" into the outer coating of the wire to see inside. As Employee #1 was
cutting into the coating, his tool came into contact with the energized internal
wire. Employee #2 was shocked while attempting to remove the employee from the
wire. Employee #1 died due to being electrocuted, and Employee #2 sustained
burns to his hands.
At 12:00 p.m. on October 5, 2024, an employee was conducting roofing work by
adding shingles while working on a window overhang. The employee lost footing
and fell approximately 22 feet, striking his head on the ground. The fall
resulted in fatal injuries.
At 4:00 p.m. on November 20, 2024, an employee working for a family vineyard was
located outside a vineyard gate. A police officer that was passing by saw the
employee on the ground unresponsive. The employee died from a possible heart
attack.
At 12:00 p.m. on November 21, 2024, an employee was working from the second tier
of a two-tiered scaffold using a winch to lift and place concrete panels into a
fence system. The employee moved the winch to the front left corner of the
scaffold to place a panel on a taller fence section. The weight on the corner
caused the scaffold to become unbalanced and topple over. The employee fell and
struck his head on a concrete traffic divider, sustaining fatal head fractures.
At 2:21 p.m. on November 22, 2024, an employee was working as a truck driver for
a contractor that provides crane and rigging services and heavy load
transportation. The employee was standing on the backside of a trailer truck in
power company yard. A coworker (crane operator) was moving a 50-foot,
3,182-pound power pole onto the trailer using a Manitex Model 3051T Series C
mobile truck crane. The coworker was attempting to move the power pole load
while the employee was standing near the truck to guiding the load. The employee
did not approve of how the pole was being loaded onto the truck. As the coworker
moved the load on the trailer, the pole began tilting into a vertical position.
The rigging failed allowing the pole to slip out of the sling. The pole bounced
and struck the employee causing him to fall off the back of the truck and onto
the asphalt ground striking his head. The employee died from crush injuries and
head trauma.
On November 19, 2024, an employee working for a specialty mulch manufacturer was
cleaning and performing maintenance along with three coworkers. The crew was
working on a catwalk on the roof of the plant. The employee stepped off of the
catwalk and fell through a skylight approximately 20 feet. The employee landed
on a baling machine and fell to the concrete floor below.  The employee was
transported by ambulance and helicopter to the hospital where he was admitted to
the ICU with significant head trauma and a possible hip injury.  On November 22,
2024, the employer reported that the employee was taken off life support and
died later the same day.
At 3:36 p.m. on November 20, 2024, an employee who worked in shipping for a rice
manufacturer was tasked with loading and probing a railcar with rice. The
employee was working with a team of  four quality control coworkers, which
included the supervisor. The team was sealing the railcars for shipping the next
day. Two coworkers sealed the railcars from the ground and the other two
coworker, including the supervisor, went on top to seal the railcars from the
top. Another coworker, the mobile track operator, sounded the horn and started
moving the railcars. The employee was still connected by his fall protection
system, so he started to walk towards the incoming railcar as it gained speed
attempting to transition from one to the other. The employee was pulled by the
SLR and was not able to make the transition between railcars. The employee fell
in the gap between the railcars and was crushed by the wheels. The employee died
from amputations to both lower legs.
At 9:00 a.m. on November 7, 2024, an employee working as the chief financial
officer for a township had arrived at work. The employee reported feeling
unwell. Shortly after sitting at her desk, the  employee lost consciousness and
was transported to the hospital. The employee died a short time later from
natural causes possibly related to her cardiovascular system.
At 4:15 p.m. an employee who worked as a welder for a rock products manufacturer
was sitting down waiting to clock out. The employee collapsed and died from
cardiac arrest.
At 12:00 a.m. on July 30, 2021, Employee #1 was working at a hosiery mill and
was standing on top of a dryer, installing a rim, when he slipped and fell to
the concrete floor. The fall was greater than eight feet. He was evaluated the
same day at a clinic and diagnosed with a closed displaced intertrochanteric
fracture of the left femur. He was then transferred to a hospital for a higher
level of care. On July 31, 2021, he underwent surgery to repair the hip fracture
and was discharged without complication on August 1, 2021.  According to family
members, the employee had been recovering well until the morning of August 12,
2021, when he experienced sudden shortness of breath. A family member returned
home at approximately 12:50 p.m. to find him unresponsive on a waterbed.
Emergency services were called, and upon arrival, found the employee pulseless
and apneic. Despite 30 minutes of resuscitative efforts-including
defibrillation, epinephrine administration, and intubation-he was pronounced
dead at 1:43 p.m. on August 12, 2021.  Initial documentation attributed the
death to complications of the femur fracture. However, a family-requested
autopsy later revealed the cause of death to be heart disease, including an
enlarged heart, severe pericardial adhesions, acute myocardial infarction, and
coronary artery disease.
At 4:10 p.m. on November 25, 2024, an employee working at a slaughterhouse was
working on a schedule that allowed him to acclimate to the environment. The
employee was attempting to qualify to the 80 percent work and 20 percent rest
cycle (80/20), but was still working at a 60/40 cycle. The employee's position
required him to remove the butt hide section of a carcass using an air knife.
At 12:00 a.m. on January 31, 2025, an employee was walking from his tractor,
when he was struck by a switcher vehicle being operated by another employee. He
was transported to the hospital and admitted for treatment for a broken leg and
other unknown injuries. The employee later died at the hospital.
On February 18, 2025, Employee #1 was a surveyor working on a crew with three
coworkers. The crew was tasked with surveying land for an expansion project near
an interstate highway. The employee was working alone, standing behind Coworker
#1's truck,  setting up work zone signs on the shoulder of the road. An
18-wheeler driving by Employee #1, experienced a tire failure, causing a tire to
detach from the vehicle. The tire struck Employee #1 and hit the work vehicle
parked on the side of the road. Employee #1 sustained fatal injuries.
At 8:38 a.m. on February 19, 2025, Employee #1 was walking at a worksite when he
was struck  by a front-end loader. The employee sustained fatal injuries.
At 5:45 p.m. on February 3, 2025,  Employee #1 attempted to charge a dead
vehicle battery on the second level of a car carrier.  He fell through an open
space where a vehicle would normally be positioned and sustained fatal injuries.
At 9:36 a.m. on June 5, 2024, Employee #1 was performing tree removal while
working from the bucket of an articulating boom tree care vehicle. The employee
extended the boom too far, which caused the left outrigger support to lift off
the ground, resulting in the vehicle overturning onto its side. Employee #1 fell
approximately 75 feet to compacted soil and sustained a fractured skull and
dislocated neck at the spinal cord, resulting in a fatality.
At 8:15 a.m. on February 17, 2025,  Employee #1 was connecting a steam hose to
the steam valve of railcar to reheat and pump soybean oil. After partially
opening the steam valve to allow gradual heating, the railcar suddenly imploded
and collapsed downward, striking the employee. The employee sustained fatal
injuries.
At 2:00 p.m. on February 18, 2025, Employee #1 was working for a roofing
contractor and was installing insulation on a roof. Employee #1 fell from a
21-foot elevation  Employee #1 sustained fatal injuries.
At 8:34 a.m. on February 20, 2025, Employee #1 and coworkers were closing a
steel door mounted on a railing system with track wheels. While manually
adjusting the door, one of the track wheels came off the rail, causing the door
to jackknife. Three employees were on the door attempting to realign it when the
door fell backward, trapping Employee #1 in the middle.  Employee #1 sustained
fatal injuries.
At 7:27 p.m. on February 19, 2025, Employee #1 was installing decking on the
upper level of a metal structure.  The employee fell and sustained fatal
injuries.
At 6:00 a.m. on December 3, 2024, Employee #1 lost consciousness while reporting
to work. The employee was found unresponsive and subsequently died.
At 1:00 p.m. on February 20, 2025, Employee #1 was  tasked with loading vehicles
into another container.  While attaching metal wires to secure the vehicle
wheels inside the container, one of the wires snapped, causing a vehicle to fall
and strike Employee #1.  Employee #1 was fatally injured.
At 8:30 a.m. on February 21, 2025, Employee #1 was working as a construction
trades helper for a general building contractor and was ensuring that a vertical
mullion was level. Employee #1 was attempting to hand a tool to a coworker who
was on an aerial lift. The mullion broke free and the employee fell, sustaining
fatal injuries.
At 10:55 a.m. on February 17, 2025,  Employee #1 was working  in a 5.5-foot-wide
by 7-foot-deep trench lubricating a water pipe for a water project. Employee #1
was tasked with preparing the water pipes so they could be connected. He kneeled
down to lubricate a pipe when the right side of the trench collapsed trapping
the employee. Employee #1 was fatally injured.
At 3:00 p.m. on February 20, 2025, a rigging crew was walking up a road line to
reach the landing area. A large chunk of wood broke loose from the landing and
rolled downhill, striking an employee. The employee sustained fatal injuries.
At 12:25 p.m. on February 24, 2025,  Employee #1 was working as a roofer at a
warehouse worksite and was engaged in roof removal. Coworker #2 (driver) was
operating a roll-off truck, Employee #1 was standing between the roll-off truck
and the west side of the building in front of loading dock removing roofing
debris from the ground around the loading dock. Coworker #2 repositioned the
truck and requested that the area where the container would be placed be cleared
of debris.  Employee #1 and Coworker #3 gave a thumbs-up indicating the area was
clear. Coworker #2 began lowering the container.  The hook securing the
container detached during the lowering process. Coworker #2 reattached the
cable, lifted the container back onto the truck, and discovered  Employee #1
lying on the ground behind the truck. The employee was caught between the
40-yard roll-off container and building.  Employee #1 sustained fatal injuries.
At 8:00 a.m. on February 10, 2025, Employee #1 was using an acetylene torch to
cut a piece of steel, resting the material on two empty methanol barrels.
Residual vapor or liquid inside one of the barrels ignited, causing a
deflagration.  Employee #1 was struck and sustained fatal injuries.
At 9:00 a.m. on February 20,2025, Employee #1 and Coworker #1 were working as
masons and had begun to manually dig a trench with a shovel while trying to find
a concrete footer attached to the foundation of a house. They were instructed
to dig down until they found the footer and then to continue lengthwise.
Employee #1 and Coworker #1 remained in the trench and continued digging.
Employee #1 was at the left side of the trench, and Coworker #1 was on the right
side. The depth on the left side was approximately 8 to 9 feet and the depth on
the right side was approximately 5 feet. The left side of the trench collapsed
causing dirt to engulf Employee #1.  The employee was fatally injured.
At 12:00 p.m. on February 22, 2025,  Employee #1 and Employee #2  were working
approximately 250 feet above the ground while repairing blades on a windmill.
The workers ascended on a suspended scaffold that indicated the primary cable
rigging was only attached at one end. This allowed the sling to slip free as the
scaffold ascended causing the full weight of the scaffold to transfer to the
second cable.  The secondary cable should have acted as a brake and locked the
scaffold in place. However, the scaffold fell approximately 20 feet before the
secondary cable seized and snapped due to the momentum, causing the scaffold to
fall. Both employees sustained fatal injuries.
At 1:00 p.m. on February 21, 2025, employees were unloading palletized granite
slabs from the back of a truck using a forklift. The granite slabs began to
lean, and three employees attempted to correct the hazard. The slabs then fell,
pinning one employee between the fallen granite and another pallet. The employee
sustained fatal injuries and another employee was seriously injured and
hospitalized.
At 4:48 p.m. on February 19, 2025, Employee #1 was operating a reach truck to
remove a pallet from a storage rack approximately 22 feet high. While
maneuvering the reach truck within the aisle, the employee leaned out of the
safety cage area.  Employee #1 became caught between the rear vertical overhead
guard support and a lower rack metal support post behind him. Employee #1
sustained fatal injuries.
At 6:45 a.m. on February 24, 2025, Employee #1 was working as a construction
laborer and was tearing down a hotel entrance canopy. The canopy also served as
a carport for arriving guests. Employee #1 was under the canopy when it suddenly
collapsed. Employee #1 was fatally injured.
At 6:30 p.m. on February 13, 2025, Employee #1 was traveling to feed and water
horses while driving an ATV. Employee #1 sustained fatal injuries.
At 2:49 p.m. on February 22, 2025, Employee #1 was standing on a 5-foot ladder
inspecting a sandblasting tank while refilling it and checking hose connections.
An unidentified substance inside the tank exploded, causing Employee #1 to be
thrown from the ladder.  Employee #1 was fatally injured.
At 11:00 a.m. on February 22, 2025,  Employee #1 was laying out walkway
handrails on the floor in preparation for installation on top of the coldbox
project. While on a ladder checking and securing bolts on the handrails, the
employee was struck by an overhead crane. The employee sustained fatal injuries.
At 11:43 a.m. on February 24, 2025,  Employee #1 was spray painting aircraft
parts while wearing a supplied air respirator. Nitrogen back flowed into the
breathing air system, displacing oxygen and causing the employee to be
asphyxiated.  Employee #1 was fatally injured.
At approximately 10:30 a.m. on February 22, 2025, Employee #1 was cutting the
top portion of a 40-foot tree while working from an elevated truck-mounted
bucket. During the operation, the tree fell toward the bucket and struck the
employee.  Employee #1 sustained fatally injuries.
At approximately 9:30 a.m. on February 25, 2025,  Employee #1 was using a chain
saw to cut a section of a tree trunk that was lying horizontally with its root
ball positioned vertically, 90 degrees to the ground. After the trunk section
was cut, the root ball rotated and returned to a vertical position, striking the
ground with its roots. The impact caused another tree to fall, and it struck the
employee. Employee #1 sustained fatal injuries.
At approximately 5:00 p.m. on February 23, 2025, Employee #1 was working from a
spider basket aerial lift. After completing part of the task,  Employee #1
prepared to relocate to another area, which required additional rigging
equipment, including a 21-inch cable wire with 5/16-inch hooks. A temporary line
was used during the relocation. While the basket was being repositioned, it fell
approximately 80 feet into a body of water. Employee #1 was fatally injured.
